tour.overview:
Tulum was a walled Maya port, flourishing between the 13th and 15th centuries, set on cliffs above a beach of white sand and turquoise sea, one of the most photographed sites in Mexico. Inland, Cobá was a much older and larger city, hidden in the jungle, with a network of raised white roads, the sacbeob, and the tall Nohoch Mul pyramid. The limestone of the Yucatán is riddled with cenotes, sinkholes filled with crystal-clear water, which the Maya saw as gateways to the underworld.

This private day combines them with a licensed guide and a vehicle.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 9 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Cancún, Playa del Carmen or Tulum
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, vehicle and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy to moderate

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Tulum ruins.
• Cobá.
• Two cenotes.
• A Maya community.

WHY THIS WORKS
Starting at Tulum when it opens avoids the crowds and the heat, and the private vehicle links the scattered sites.

WHO IT SUITS
Families, couples, swimmers and history lovers.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For Chichén Itzá, choose our Chichén Itzá, cenote and Valladolid tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Climbing Nohoch Mul is currently not allowed. Use biodegradable sun cream only, or none, in the cenotes.

days.name: Tulum, cenotes, Cobá by bicycle and lunch with a Maya family
days.description:
What to expect: the coast and jungle of the Maya world, with a licensed guide, private vehicle, entrances, bicycles, cenotes and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you early and drive to Tulum, arriving at opening time. Inside the walls, you see El Castillo on the edge of the cliff, the Temple of the Descending God and the Temple of the Frescoes, with traces of painted murals, while iguanas bask on the stones and the sea glitters below.

You then swim and snorkel in a cenote, perhaps Gran Cenote or a quieter one, in clear water among stalactites and small fish. In the jungle, you explore Cobá by bicycle or by tricycle taxi along the ancient sacbeob, to the ball court, the carved stelae and the Nohoch Mul pyramid, some 42 metres high, rising above the trees.

Lunch is with a Maya family in a nearby village, with handmade tortillas and local dishes, and a chance to learn about their customs and the Maya language. A second cenote, hidden in the jungle, offers a final swim before you return to your hotel.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:00 – Pick-up (Playa del Carmen).
08:00 – Tulum ruins.
10:00 – First cenote.
11:30 – Cobá by bicycle.
13:30 – Lunch with a Maya family.
15:00 – Second cenote.
17:00 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• A beach stop at Tulum can replace the second cenote.
• Akumal, to swim with sea turtles, can be added.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, licensed guide, entrances, bicycles, cenotes and equipment, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: drinks, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Can we climb the pyramid at Cobá?
faq.answer: Climbing Nohoch Mul is currently not permitted.

faq.question: Do we need to swim well for the cenotes?
faq.answer: No; life vests are available, and many cenotes are shallow in parts.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the bicycles and the cenotes.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. Tricycle taxis are available at Cobá; cenotes have steps.

faq.question: Can we add Akumal?
faq.answer: Yes, to snorkel with sea turtles.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: Can we bring sun cream?
faq.answer: Only biodegradable, or none, in the cenotes.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Swimwear, light clothes, a hat, comfortable shoes and insect repellent.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: November to April; summer is hot and humid.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is customary in Mexico: 10 to 15 percent for guides and drivers is usual if you were happy with the service, but it is always your choice.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
